SAVINGS-DONT TOUCH is a staging account rather than savings — money arrives and leaves within days, and it earned $0.11 over 18 months. The Wise figure is $83.84 CAD plus $86.82 USD, converted at the 0.7112 rate actually paid rather than a spot rate, and is calculated from the transaction ledger rather than read off Wise.

netWorth.caveat: Household net worth is now estimable. At the owner's estimate of $1.1m–$1.4m for the home, it is roughly $357,000 to $657,000 [ESTIMATE] — the financial accounts above, plus the home, less all debt. Loan-to-value on the mortgage and HELOC together ($747,612.74) is 68% at the low end and 53% at the high end, both comfortably under the 80% that matters at the May 2027 renewal. This is an owner's estimate, not an appraisal, and a lender will use its own. Vehicles, pensions and the business are still excluded.

helocSummary: Balance grew $7,536.96 over 18 months despite $78,177 of repayments, because $86,514 was advanced and $15,029 of interest was capitalised. Since the February 2026 paydown it has risen every month — +$13,525.55 in six.

cashflow.note: Bonus plus a strong resale month

cashflowNote: Nine of eighteen complete months were negative. The year balances only because two or three large months carry it. Excludes payments made directly from the HELOC — roughly $1,960/month — so the real picture is somewhat weaker than shown.
incomeNote: Her Tennis BC employment — 43 deposits, $63,129.47 over 18 months into DEBT&PAYMENTS — was absent from the earlier picture entirely, which saw only the $21,700 she transferred across. That transfer has been removed as an income line: it is an internal movement out of this income, and counting both would double it. Two cautions remain: at least $1,639.10 marked EXP is expense reimbursement rather than pay, a further $2,846.58 marked AP is unresolved, and the transfers stopped after May 2026 while the income did not.
spendingNote: Household spending averages about $7,551/month over 18 months. Roughly 19% could not be reliably categorised — TD truncates merchant names. This total is still incomplete: $9,930 of Amazon Mastercard purchases and $6,760 on the two TD Visas are captured but not yet folded into any category.

questions.detail: $54,213 of inbound e-transfers over 18 months against $23,200 outbound, $13,062 of it drawn from the HELOC at 4.90%. Heavy retail purchasing currently counted as household spending. A CRA balance paid from the HELOC.
questions.changes: Everything. Whether household spending is overstated, whether HELOC growth is working capital or leakage, and what the tax position is.

questions.q: Where do the "credit card" transfers go?
questions.detail: $46,657 over 18 months. The TD Visa's balance fell only $391 in that time and shows no purchases at all.
questions.changes: Could reveal a card with a significant balance entirely absent from the debt ranking.

questions.detail: $747,613 of debt is secured against it. Original mortgage $648,000 in May 2022.
questions.changes: Net worth is unstateable without it, and loan-to-value decides what is possible at the May 2027 renewal.

questions.q: Where does the rest of the $19,700 of e-transfers go?
questions.detail: $3,500 is now traced to the Wise holiday accounts. The remainder still leaves the household without a matched destination, $13,062 of it originally drawn from the HELOC.
questions.changes: The working theory is business inventory. If so it is a business cost currently counted as household spending, and it is being funded by borrowing against the house.

questions.q: Why did the monthly transfer stop after May 2026?
questions.detail: $1,000/month from March 2025, stepping to $1,100 in November, reliable through May 2026. Absent since.
questions.changes: About $1,100/month, and whether the budget needs rebuilding.

questions.q: What are the two unidentified accounts?
questions.detail: One sent $33,598 across 142 transfers; the other received $16,945 across five.
questions.changes: $59,027 of movement, likely folding into question 1.
